Paris Jackson has shared that her brief but memorable tribute at her father Michael Jackson’s memorial service happened “in the moment.”

Paris was just 11 years old when her legendary father died at his Los Angeles home from cardiac arrest as a result of a propofol overdose in June 2009. She famously stepped up to the microphone inside Los Angeles’ packed Staples Center and spoke just a few sentences at the King of Pop’s memorial service, which was being broadcast live across the U.S.

“Ever since I was born, Daddy has been the best father you could ever imagine,” Paris said on stage, flanked by her aunts Janet and La Toya Jackson. “And I just want to say I love him so much,” she added before dissolving into tears and being ushered offstage by her family.

Looking back on the moment during Wednesday’s episode of the Call Her Daddy podcast, Paris revealed her speech was unplanned.

“Oh, it kind of just happened in the moment,” she told host Alex Cooper. “It was kind of like, yeah, I’ve been on stage where it was like, they looked and they’re like, ‘Are one of the kids going to say something?’ And no one moved. So I was like, f*** it, we ball. And ... yeah, it just happened.”

open image in gallery Paris Jackson stepped up to the microphone at just 11 years old to pay tribute to her dad, Michael, at his memorial service in 2009 ( Getty )

open image in gallery Jackson revealed that her speech at her dad’s funeral was unplanned during the latest episode of ‘Call Her Daddy’ ( AFP/Getty )

Asked by Cooper whether she felt any pressure in that moment, Paris responded: “Well, because when eyes turn and they’re like, ‘Someone’s got to say something.’ ... I have not gone back to watch it to see how quickly it all happened, but it felt like it happened very slowly. And it felt like someone’s got to say something.

“Little bro’s not going to do it. Older bro’s not moving,” she added, referring to her two siblings, Prince, 29, and Bigi, 24.

Paris, 28, has continued to advocate for her father in the years since his death, most notably with an ongoing legal battle over his estate. She and her brothers are the beneficiaries of Michael’s estate, which is now estimated to be worth over $2 billion.

Michael’s only daughter raised concerns last July about executors John Branca and John McClain allegedly mishandling the late singer’s money after reportedly noticing irregular payments. She went on to accuse the attorneys of “skimming money” from her father’s estate.

Branca and McClain have denied all allegations against them.

Earlier this year, a Los Angeles judge ruled in favor of Paris, deciding that the money will have to be returned to the estate. The ruling also demanded transparency in the way that the Jackson family’s money is spent.

News.title: Madagascar forced to divide and share mpox vaccine as epidemic takes off
News.content:
Authorities in Madagascar are being forced to split single vaccines into fifths to try to protect as many people as possible during an ongoing mpox outbreak.

The method, known as “fractional dosing”, is authorised by the World Health Organization (WHO) in emergencies when there are critical vaccine shortages, but is not routinely recommended and carries a level of risk.

Madagascar, the African island with a population of roughly 33 million people, is currently battling its largest-ever outbreak of the virus formerly known as monkeypox, with at least 4,000 cases recorded so far.

Another one million people are thought to be at risk of contracting clade 1b mpox, a fast-spreading strain of the virus that emerged from the Democratic Republic of the Congo in late 2023.

High risk groups include sex workers, young children, and people living with HIV/Aids. Medical workers are also at risk.

“Public health authorities in Madagascar have been given too few doses to protect the at-risk population; they were initially given 30,000 doses in May, and a subsequent 30,000 have just arrived at the end of July,” said Akhil Bansal, a doctor of internal medicine working on the mpox response in Madagascar and a policy fellow at the Centre for Global Development.

“However, we need to vaccinate more than one million people, so we have been “fractionally dosing”, or splitting vaccines, into fifths, to stretch the supply as far as we can.

“This is a somewhat established approach for vaccines, but even then, the number of doses we have is insufficient,” said Dr Bansal.

News.title: Sudan exodus threatens humanitarian catastrophe in Chad
News.content:
Trapped in a desert encampment in Chad, Abakar Adam, 70, dreams of returning to his small farm in neighbouring Sudan, nearby to the village where he was born.

But Mr Adam can’t go home.

Hidden from sight, he watched soldiers set fire to his farmhouse and slaughter his livestock three years ago. One month later, after resettling in the city of El Geneina in West Darfur he heard 40mm grenades rain down on hospitals while patients fought for their lives inside and witnessed civilians executed in the street.

Shortly after, a bullet from the rifle of a Rapid Support Force (RSF) soldier ripped through his gut, and he recalls how he struggled to pull his daughter from the blood-soaked sand after her eye was gouged out by a militiaman during their escape from Sudan.

Now, sitting outside his rotting, wooden shelter in eastern Chad, just 20 miles from the border with Sudan, he tells The Telegraph that he can’t forget the faces of the blind and disabled who he witnessed being thrown onto piles of hay and burnt alive.

Adam’s story is not unique and the refugee camp where he finds himself with tens of thousands of others is on the brink of collapse.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football 2026/27: Everything you need to know and FAQs
News.content:
What’s new for 2026/27?





You’ll need to re-register

When signing up to Telegraph Fantasy Football this season you will notice your old logins do not work.

New for this season you will need to register, or login to an existing, telegraph.co.uk account to play.

NOTE: you do not need to subscribe in order to play Telegraph Fantasy Football - it is free to play.

Having trouble making a new account or logging in to an existing telegraph.co.uk account? Click here and look at our troubleshooting guide that can guide you through the process.



We’ve had a makeover and Leagues have moved

Over the summer we changed game provider meaning the site was built again from scratch. We hope you like the new look and feel.

We know nobody likes change, but take your time to get to know the new layout as some aspects of the site may have moved slightly.

The most notable change is that Leagues are now created and joined below your team selection.



Back to basics

With such a short space of time to get the TFF live for this season, the game has been stripped back to basics.

You’ll notice there are no Public Leagues and no prizes for Weekly and Monthly Leaderboard winners. Assistant Manager has also not been integrated for launch.



The Fixture Tracker

Whilst the game has been stripped back to basics, you’ll notice a new fixture tracker above your team selection. This is there to help you make transfer decisions and we hope you like it.

When you see a + in the tracker it indicates how many other games start at that time.



No rule changes.

Whilst some things may have changed, the rules remain unchanged.

Telegraph Fantasy Football is fantasy football at its purest. No gimmicks, no boosts, no captains. Simply pick the best XI players you can.



Assists

However, one exception is this season assists will no longer follow Opta’s “Fantasy Assist” definition and revert back to standard assists.



Did you miss it? League Cup fixtures and five more transfers

In case you missed it last year, this season will also feature League Cup fixtures meaning all competitive domestic football containing Premier League fixtures will count towards your Telegraph Fantasy Football points tally.

Why the change? Well for years the general advice early in the season is to hold onto your transfers and we thought that was getting a bit stale. With League Cup fixtures starting as early as Game Week 3 some seasons, you’d be a fool not to take advantage of some fixture gains against lower-league opposition.

To help with the additional fixtures we have also added five more transfers to your season total.



Paid leagues are no more

Unfortunately Plucky Paid Leagues are not integrated this season.



Three new teams

Ipswich are no strangers to Telegraph Fantasy Football as they both return from relegations in 2025. They bring with them a host of talent including two big names you might recognise, including Jaden Philogene (£2.9m) and Leif Davis (£2.6m).

It has been a fair few years since Hull City (2016/17) and Coventry City (2000/01) last featured in Telegraph Fantasy Football - memories may even flood back of posting in your transfers for the Sky Blues’ players. Both clubs are favourites to go down, but with some exciting signings like Tzolakis (£2.5m) and Thomas-Asante (£2.7m) they will certainly put up a fight.

Start creating your team >



FAQs





When does Telegraph Fantasy Football start?

The 2026/27 edition of Telegraph Fantasy Football will launch in the two weeks leading up to the start of the Premier League. The scoring will commence on Friday August 21, 2026 at 8pm when the Premier League champions Arsenal host Coventry.



How do I register for Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You will need to create a new, or use your existing telegraph.co.uk account in order to play Telegraph Fantasy Football. Simply click “SIGN UP”, then “Continue with Telegraph” and you will be temporarily taken to telegraph.co.uk to login with your existing Telegraph account or create a new account, before automatically returning back to the Telegraph Fantasy Football site.

Note: this account is not the same as your account from previous Telegraph Fantasy Football seasons.

Having trouble making a new account or logging in to an existing telegraph.co.uk account? Click here and look at our troubleshooting guide that can guide you through the process.



How much does it cost to play Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Telegraph Fantasy Football is completely free to play. All managers compete for the £5,000 prize pool as well the chance to challenge friends, family, colleagues and fellow managers in private mini-leagues.



How many players can I pick in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You only have to pick a squad of XI players in Telegraph Fantasy Football. With no bench to rely on, finding players who get minutes on the pitch is key and we help you out there by allowing transfers right up until every kick-off.



How many teams can I pick in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You can create up to five teams in Telegraph Fantasy Football with a budget of £50m for each, meaning you have a better chance of being in contention for the prizes come the end of the season if some of your selections prove to be unsuccessful.



How many transfers can I make in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Up until the first game on Friday August 21, 2025, there is a transfer amnesty, meaning you can make as many changes as you like. After the season has started you have 45 transfers for the whole campaign with a maximum of five per Game Week (00:00 Tuesday to 23:59 Monday).





How do I join a private league in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Leagues have now moved below your team selection.

This should make it easier for managers to see which league the team is in that they are making changes to.

To join a league click “Join a league” and then add the 6 digit code that the League Chairman will have access to.

To create a league click “Create a league”, name the league and then copy the league code generated to share with your fellow managers.

League Chairmen will have the ability to lock and unlock a league to new joiners.



Do ALL Cup games count in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Yes. All League Cup fixtures plus all FA Cup games involving Premier League sides count towards your TFF points tally. This adds a great dimension to the game as you will want to load your teams with players who make the latter stages for an advantage over your competitors. However, one thing to note is that penalty shoot-outs do not count towards your score.



How many players are in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You can expect to compete against more than 100,000 other teams in Telegraph Fantasy Football – a vast but tight-knit community of players where you have every chance of winning one of our many prizes on offer throughout the year.

We aim to include every player in a squad who has a chance of getting some game time. From time to time we may miss a youngster on debut, but rest assured they will soon be added to the player list and feel free to let us know on Facebook or Twitter if you feel someone is missing.

Having technical issues with TFF? Check our Troubleshooting page for help.



What else do I need to know?



Get your strategy right. Getting the balance of your team right can be a tricky business, especially with limited funds, but there are a few tried and trusted methods that will stand you in good stead:



Pick regular starters

Okay, so this isn’t always straightforward in the world of squad rotation where world-class players routinely find themselves sitting on the bench. That said, there are certain players who, if fit, are almost always the first name on the team sheet. Think Bruno Fernandes at Manchester United, Jordan Pickford for Everton and Liverpool’s Virgil van Dijk.



Find a couple of budget ‘gems’

Igor Thiago, Nico O’Reilly and James Garner were among a crop of players who began last term in the ‘unfancied’ category and were must-have ‘enablers’ by the time the season was over. If you’re able to identify one or two of this type of player early in the season, you could be on to a winner.



Be transfer savvy

We’ve all been there – you spend hours selecting your team for the big kick-off then half of them don’t start, the other half have stinkers and your star striker gets a season-ending injury. If you do get off to a slow start, don’t panic. Lurching from one strategy to another could do more harm than good, wasting precious transfers in the process. Trust your instincts, tweak where necessary and the points will come.



Read our weekly Selection Guide

The best advice comes from experts at the Fantasy Football Hub who make our weekly selection guide a prolific source of Telegraph Fantasy Football tips and Telegraph Fantasy Football match facts.

If you subscribe to the weekly newsletter this will hit your inbox on Friday around lunchtime; alternatively it can be found on our social channels or Telegraph Fantasy Football content hub.



Telegraph Fantasy Football Player List

We aim to keep our player list up to date with all comings and goings in the transfer window and the first place to look is our trusted Stats Centre. However, if you fancy yourself as a bit of a Telegraph Fantasy Football expert like the team at Fantasy Football Hub, you can find a player list below in a spreadsheet format so you can do your own analysis.

On the document simply click “file”, then “make a copy” and you will have your own version of the player list at that time to edit as you please.



Download the Telegraph Fantasy Football App

Never miss a chance to make a transfer and download the Telegraph Fantasy Football App which is available on iOS and Android.





You can follow the latest Telegraph Fantasy Football news and discussions throughout the year on Facebook, Twitter and Fantasy Football Content Hub.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football: transfers explained and top transfer tips
News.content:
As the new Telegraph Fantasy Football season approaches, the fantasy football experts at Fantasy Football Hub will continue to bring you the very best in fantasy football knowledge, tips and tools to help you rise up the ranks and win your mini-leagues.

To join the Hub and get access to all their great resources and expert tips you can take advantage of its 50% pre-season discount here.



Transfers explained



A good place to start is by explaining the Telegraph Fantasy Football rules on transfers. First thing to note is the pre-season transfer amnesty, so you can make unlimited changes to your teams right up until the first scheduled kick-off on Friday 21 August, 20:00.

45 is the magic number of transfers you receive during the season, five more than last season to help negotiate the new League Cup fixtures. This equates to a little more than one a week. You can use a maximum of five transfers in any Game Week which run from 00:00 on Tuesdays to 23:59 on Mondays.

Four seasons ago we scrapped the two-hour rule, meaning you can make transfers right up until a game kicks off. However, we don’t suggest you leave it that late as if a transfer is not completed in time you will not gain any points for the game from the player transferred in. Starting XIs are released an hour before kick-off so you have an ample window to implement any changes.

Scrapping the two-hour rule also means that this year you can be more flexible with your transfers each week. Once a player’s game has started you will amass their points for the entire game and are free to transfer them out for another player who may be kicking off while the previous game is being played, thus benefiting from two players’ points.



Top transfer strategy tips



1) Utilise fixture gains



Telegraph Fantasy Football is unique amongst other fantasy games in that you can transfer a player out as soon as they’ve played for a player yet to play that day or match week. So if Haaland (£8.3m) played in the 12.30pm Saturday kick-off, managers can transfer him out for Saka (£6.0m) who plays in the 3pm kick-off, and score points for both. Picking up extra fixtures each time a transfer is made is key to TFF success.



2) Find enablers early and stick



To fit in a combination of Erling Haaland (£8.3m), Bruno Fernandes (£6.5m) and Cole Palmer (£6.2m) or similar, requires TFF managers to find cheaper players to balance teams. Finding those players early into the season, and sticking with them to utilise transfers on the other strategy tips, can ensure avoiding wasting transfers on constant restructuring of squads.



3) FA Cup and League Cup (new for 2025/26)

Players in TFF gain points for the League Cup and FA Cup as well as the Premier League, so often players topping points charts at the season end have progressed far in the competition. When seeing lineups for early League Cup and FA Cup Rounds, if big hitting players who are regulars in the league start against lowly opposition, it’s a prime opportunity to stock up on those assets.

New for this season League Cup fixtures have been included which will make the early stages of the season even more exciting when Premier League teams who are not competing in Europe will gain a fixture against the rest.



4) Favourable fixture runs

Picking players who are playing against weaker opposition often score more points, therefore keeping an eye on the fixtures for teams is important.



5) Balance transfers out over the season

There are ~37 gameweeks in the season, so averaging around one transfer a week is a rule of thumb that keeps managers from running out early. The start of the season is the only time your team is reset, so it’s important to set a structure that works for you so that you don’t need to use too many moves at the start to identify those players who are likely to shine. It’s a marathon, not a sprint, so keeping pace early isn’t a necessity, and often keeping a few extra back until the end run sees TFF managers get a late boost.



Pick your free Telegraph Fantasy Football team now >

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football points: a complete guide to scoring
News.content:
How many points for a Goal?

A regular source of goals is often the first thing a manager looks for in a fantasy football team. The highly-priced Erling Haaland is a go-to signing for many, but last season saw the continuation of mid-priced forwards getting in on the action too with the likes of Igor Thiago racking up 22 goals in Telegraph Fantasy Football.

Players get five points per goal scored which, added to starting appearance points (two), mean a regularly starting goal scorer can be a huge asset.



How many points for an Assist?

It won’t take a master tactician to work out that players who rank highly in the goalscoring charts often also feature in the upper echelons of the Assists table.

Bruno Fernandes was head and shoulders above the rest with regard to assist points last season with 21 in total (nine clear of his closest rival).

An assist will earn three points.





What counts as an Assist?

An Assist is the final touch (pass, pass-cum-shot or any other touch) leading to the recipient of the ball scoring a goal.

Outside of fantasy football, if the final touch is deflected by an opposition player, the initiator is only given a goal assist if the receiving player was likely to receive the ball without the deflection having taken place. Own goals, directly taken free kicks, direct corner goals and penalties do not get an assist awarded.

In a change to previous years, Fantasy Assists are not being used.



How many points for a Tackle?

A slightly more nuanced aspect of scoring is the points a player earns for a successful tackle. Managers will need to cast their nets wide to capitalise on tackling points as the highest scorers tend to come from mid-table and even lower-table teams.

Everton’s James Garner was a key beneficiary of tackle bonus points last season with 120 tackles in total. His closest rivals have been very popular this summer with Wolves’ Joao Gomes, now at Aston Villa, and Nottingham Forest’s Elliot Anderson, now at Manchester City. It’s clear from this that deeper lying midfielders are more likely to amass points here.

Players earn a point for every two tackles made during a match and only midfielders are eligible.



What counts as a Tackle?

A tackle is defined as a player connecting with the ball in a ground challenge and successfully taking the ball away from the player in possession. The tackled player must have clearly been in possession of the ball before the tackle was made.

The final destination of the ball (to the tackler, to a teammate, to an opposition player or out of play) is not considered. A tackle will only be deemed unsuccessful if the player tackled retains possession of the ball.

A player cutting out a pass does not count as a tackle.

Players earn a point for every two tackles made.



How many points for a Clean Sheet?

Attainable by goalkeepers and defenders, the top-scorers in the clean sheet category last season mostly came from Arsenal.

There are five clean sheet points on offer for a player who has played at least 60 minutes of a match and two points if the player has played less than an hour where the game has finished with their team conceding zero goals.



How many points for a Save?

In addition to clean sheet points, goalkeepers can earn one point for every two saves made in a match. Much like points for tackling, save points introduce a new angle to team selection with keepers from teams further down the table likely to face more shots than those who generally dominate games.



What counts as a Save?

A save is a goalkeeper preventing the ball from entering the goal with any part of his body when facing an intentional attempt to score by an opposition player.

Saves have the following attributes:

Body part: Hands/Feet/Body

Save type: Caught/Collected/Parried Safe/Parried Danger area/Fingertip

Goalkeeper position: Diving/Standing/Reaching/Stooping

News.title: Arsenal lose second successive pre-season friendly after parading Guimaraes
News.content:
Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

“I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

Sports.title: Everton player charged with 61 breaches of FA betting rules as statement released
Sports.content:
Everton player charged with 61 breaches of FA betting rules as statement released

The Football Association (FA) have charged an Everton player for breaching their betting rules as statement released and deadline to respond revealed

View Image Everton striker Martin Sherif has been charged by the Football Association

Everton Under 21s forward Martin Sherif has been charged with breaching The FA's betting rules.

‌



Sherif, 20, who hasn't made an appearance for the club's first-team but has been an unused substitute, has been accused of placing 61 bets on football matches between November 20, 2024 and February 12, 2026.

‌



The ex-Netherlands Under 17s international, who spent last season on loan at Rotherham United and then Port Vale, has been charged with breaching FA Rule E1.2, and has until Monday, August 17 to provide a response.

‌



A statement from The Football Association (FA) on Wednesday read: "Martin Sherif of Everton FC has been charged with breaching the FA's betting rules.

"It's alleged that the player breached FA Rule E1.2 in respect of 61 bets placed on football matches between 20 November 2024 and 12 February 2026. Martin Sherif has until Monday 17 August to provide a response."

‌



At this stage, it remains unclear as to which matches Sherif placed bets on during the period of time mentioned in the statement. FA rules state that there is a worldwide ban on betting on football for 'participants of clubs'.

According to the Liverpool Echo, Everton are cooperating with the FA and supporting Sherif through the process.

Sherif joined Everton's youth set-up in 2019 and began training with the first team in early 2025. But he made the loan move to League One side Rotherham last summer, scoring twice in 10 matches, but was recalled by the Toffees that December after sustaining a series of injuries.

Article continues below

In February, Sherif signed for fellow League One outfit Port Vale for the rest of the season and netted twice in 17 appearances as they were relegated. During his loan at the Valiants, he featured against Chelsea in the FA Cup quarter-final, starting his side's 7-0 defeat at Stamford Bridge.

There will be more to follow on this breaking news story and Mirror Sport will bring you the very latest updates, pictures and video as soon as possible. Please check back regularly for updates on this developing story.

Sports.title: Liverpool handed Bradley Barcola transfer boost as 'agreement nears' after PSG comments
Sports.content:
Liverpool handed Bradley Barcola transfer boost as 'agreement nears' after PSG comments

Liverpool have been in talks with Paris Saint-Germain over a deal for Bradley Barcola, and the Reds could be handed a potential boost in their pursuit of the France international

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola of Paris Saint-Germain (Image: Adam Davy/PA Wire)

Paris Saint-Germain are reportedly closing in on the signing of Barcelona star Ferran Torres, which could hand Liverpool a boost in their pursuit of Bradley Barcola. The Anfield outfit have been heavily linked with signing Barcola, 23, this summer as they look to strengthen their forward options.

‌



Liverpool have been in talks with PSG over a deal for Barcola, with the Ligue 1 giants believed to have placed a £140million valuation on the France international - a fee which the Reds are not expected to be willing to pay.

‌



Andoni Iraola is preparing for his first season as Liverpool boss, and has added three new signings to his squad, with Jeremy Jacquet and Victor Munoz arriving on permanent deals and Ronald Araujo on loan from Barcelona.

‌



Barcola remains firmly in Liverpool's sights, and a fresh development from PSG's end could now hand the Reds an encouraging boost.

Netherlands make shock move for ex-Premier League boss after Arne Slot snub READ MORE :

The Athletic have reported that PSG are on the brink of agreeing a deal to bring Ferran Torres to the club from Barcelona, though both sides are yet to finalise the specifics of the fee.

Should Torres complete his switch to PSG, the Spain international could be one of three new forwards to arrive at the reigning Champions League winners, with Maghnes Akliouche joining from Monaco and Mika Godts a target from Ajax.

‌



Consequently, a move for Torres could signal that PSG may ultimately sanction Barcola's departure before the September 1 deadline.

Barcola has been included in the PSG squad for the UEFA Super Cup clash against Aston Villa on Wednesday evening, despite reports suggesting the 23-year-old has been suffering from illness in recent days ahead of the match.

PSG boss Luis Enrique was quizzed about Barcola's future at the club, and declined to address the speculation.

‌



View 2 Images Bradley Barcola has been linked to both Liverpool and Arsenal. (Image: Jean Catuffe/Getty Images)

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Enrique said: "I don't know and I don't want to speak about any player individually, because it's always dangerous when you are asking something positive or negative about a player. I stay focused on my team."

‌



The PSG manager was also asked about a potential move for Torres, responding: "I'm not here to talk about the transfer market... only about the players who are currently at PSG."

Liverpool have two pre-season fixtures left this summer, facing Como in a double header at Anfield, before facing Newcastle United in their Premier League opener a week afterwards.

Whether Liverpool will secure any additions before the Premier League campaign kicks off remains uncertain, with Barcola's PSG teammate Ibrahim Mbaye also referenced as a possible target.

Sports.title: 8 transfers that could happen in the next week with Man Utd and Arsenal busy
Sports.content:
The Premier League's Big Six have dominated the summer transfer window so far, splashing out to raid the division for the best players.

Manchester City signed Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for £116million. Chelsea signed Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa for £117m. Tottenham signed Sandro Tonali from Newcastle for £100m. Arsenal signed Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle for £75m.

Those are among the biggest transfers of the window so far, but there are certain to be more with 20 days left until the deadline on September 1. While the past few weeks have seen intriguing deals touted - think Vinicius Junior to Arsenal, Bradley Barcola to Liverpool or Enzo Fernandez to Man City - there are plenty of others which are actually close to completion.

Here Mirror Football goes through the transfer which you can expect to see wrapped up in the next week.

‌



Tottenham hold the key to Arsenal transfer after Mikel Arteta changes target READ MORE :

Cristian Romero to Atletico Madrid

After sensational links with Arsenal, Romero is set to land at a club he appeared destined for. The Argentina international is poised to link up with his compatriot Diego Simeone in Madrid after a £34m deal was agreed with Tottenham.

Spurs have signed Marcos Senesi and Jan Paul van Hecke this summer in preparation for the sale of their captain. The 28-year-old was handed the Spurs captain's armband last summer, when he signed a new four-year contract, yet will leave following his extended post-World Cup break.

View 5 Images Cristian Romero is close to leaving Tottenham (Image: Florencia Tan Jun/UEFA via Getty Images)

Lewis Hall to Manchester United

Newcastle are trying their best to hold onto their left-back after losing Tonali, Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon. But The Sun claims that United haven't given up hope in the pursuit of their first-choice transfer target as they look to provide competition for Luke Shaw. Importantly, it is now claimed that Hall wants to join the Toon exodus and leave for Old Trafford.

‌



United are monitoring other targets, with Club Brugge's £30m-rated Joaquin Seys another option along with Jorge Salinas of Racing Santander, who could cost £14m.

View 5 Images Lewis Hall is a key target for Manchester United (Image: MI News/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

Rodri to Barcelona

The World Cup-winning captain is keen to leave Manchester City and join Barca, where he's agreed personal terms. Real Madrid remain interested in signing the Ballon d'Or winner, but Barca are in pole position, despite having seen one bid rejected already.

"Out of respect for Madrid, as they have been class, Rodri informed them that his decision is to join Barca," Rodri's agent Pablo Barquero told a Spanish radio station five days ago.

‌



City haven't given up hope of keeping Rodri yet are looking for replacements, with £85m-rated Lille star Ayyoub Bouaddi chief among them. Enzo Maresca wants a reunion with Enzo Fernandez, who Chelsea don't want to sell and have therefore slapped a £120m valuation on him.

Lamine Camara to Crystal Palace

Monaco have rejected a club-record €50m (£42m) bid from Palace for the Senegal international. Manchester United and Chelsea are reportedly monitoring Camara, a 22-year-old midfielder, but Palace will return to try and land their man.

Gabriel Jesus to Napoli

View 5 Images Gabriel Jesus is heading to the Arsenal exit (Image: Offside via Getty Images)

Jesus' agent was spotted at Napoli's training ground last week - even if he did try to pass it off as something else - and Arsenal are open to selling the Brazilian. With Romelu Lukaku and Lorenzo Lucca potentially heading for the exit, Napoli could fork out around €20m (£17m) for Jesus, who has slipped down the pecking order behind Viktor Gyokeres and Kai Havertz at Arsenal.

‌



Arsenal have so far only managed to move on Leandro Trossard (£17m to Besiktas), Jakub Kiwior (£14.7m to Porto), Karl Hein (£2.5m to Werder Bremen) and Christian Norgaard (£7m to Everton) this summer and know further exits are required.

Djed Spence to Inter Milan

Spence shot to prominence during the World Cup, yet has an uncertain future at Spurs, who have signed Andy Robertson on a free transfer and have Pedro Porro, Destiny Udogie, Souza and Ben Davies as full-back options.

Positive talks took place between Spurs and Inter Milan on Tuesday and the Italian side reportedly believe a total package of around £30m (€35m) could be enough to land the versatile defender. They want a player capable of playing wing-back and Spence appears to fit the bill.

View 5 Images Djed Spence will leave Spurs this summer (Image: Eston Parker/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images)

‌



Julio Enciso to Ipswich

Gary O'Neil managed Enciso at Chelsea's sister club Strasbourg last season and wants the Paraguayan to follow him to Suffolk. The Tractor Boys are understood to have reached an agreement for the 22-year-old, who previously spent time on loan with the club in 2025.

His fee could surpass the club-record £24m they paid Toulouse for Emersonn earlier this summer.

Matteo Ruggeri to Aston Villa

Villa have sold Lucas Digne to Paris Saint-Germain and want Ruggeri as his replacement at left-back. They have made significant progress over a deal which should be worth around £21.4m (€25m).

Ruggeri's departure to Birmingham could free up the funds required for Atleti to sign Romero.

‌

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino eyes another huge World Cup change to secure position as FIFA chief
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino eyes another huge World Cup change to secure position as FIFA chief

FIFA President Gianni Infantino's future in the role remains uncertain, but is reportedly in favour of expanding the World Cup once again

View 2 Images FIFA president Gianni Infantino

FIFA President Gianni Infantino has reportedly expressed a willingness to support another expansion of the World Cup. It has been suggested that Infantino would be in favour of the tournament increasing from 48 to 64 teams, amid ongoing uncertainty around his future in the job.

‌



The uncertainty followed news which emerged that FIFA had proposals that would have seen them sell shares of the federation’s tournaments to private investors.

‌



The controversial scheme would have affected the men's and women's World Cups, as well as the Club World Cup, but was shelved following a substantial backlash.

‌



Infantino's future as FIFA President has been uncertain ever since the proposals emerged, with UEFA releasing statements outlining their plans to boycott the federation's major tournaments if the plans were still on the table.

Gianni Infantino cornered as three federations pile pressure on under-fire FIFA boss READ MORE :

What lies ahead for Infantino remains to be seen, but a fresh update has now emerged purporting to shed light on his position regarding the next World Cup in 2030.

The Times has reported that Infantino would support expanding the tournament once more to accommodate 64 teams, despite the World Cup already having grown from 32 to 48 teams for this summer's competition in North America.

‌



The report suggests that Infantino travelled to Colombia on Friday to attend the inauguration of the country's new president, Abelardo de la Espriella, where discussions over a potential expansion of the World Cup are said to have taken place.

The 2030 World Cup will once again be shared across multiple nations, with Spain, Portugal and Morocco serving as the primary hosts, while Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay will each stage a single match to mark the competition's 100th anniversary.

View 2 Images US President Donald Trump has offered his support to Gianni Infantino (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The proposals to expand the World Cup to 64 teams were put forward by CONMEBOL, South America's governing football body, with reports suggesting Infantino is prepared to put his support behind the plans as he looks to secure the backing of more nations to secure his presidency.

With Infantino's position shrouded in uncertainty, US President Donald Trump took to Truth Social on Monday to make his feelings abundantly clear, insisting it would be an error to remove the current FIFA chief.

‌



"FIFA would be making a terrible mistake if, for any reason, they even considered replacing President Gianni Infantino,” Trump wrote.

"He is fantastic, having just presided over the most successful World Cup, by four times, ever presented.

"If he is gone, it will never be as successful or profitable again!"

Sports.title: Manchester City sign £2m goalkeeper who destroyed Man Utd's hopes of European trophy
Sports.content:
Manchester City sign £2m goalkeeper who destroyed Man Utd's hopes of European trophy

Leeds United spent big to take James Trafford to Elland Road as their new No.1 but with Gianluigi Donnarumma in situ at the Etihad, they've turned to an experienced Argentine international for cover

View Image Geronimo Rulli celebrates at the end of the 2021 UEFA Europa League final (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Manchester City have completed the signing of Argentine international Geronimo Rulli in a £2m deal.

‌



The goalkeeper has joined City from Marseille on a two-year-deal that will keep him at the Etihad until 2028. Rulli is expected to provide back-up to No.1 Gianluigi Donnarumma.

‌



The former Ajax and Villarreal star once famously scored in a penalty shootout before making the decisive save, as Villarreal won the 2021 Europa League final against Manchester United. He has won eight caps for Argentina and was part of the squad which won the World Cup in Qatar in 2022.

‌



He said: “This is an amazing opportunity for me - and one I had to grasp. When the chance to join Manchester City comes along you have to go for it. Everyone knows what an impressive club this is. City’s success over a long time has been impressive. Everyone I have spoken to about City said I had to join them because they are a club with incredibly high standards.

"Every professional wants to be in a high-performance environment and I can’t wait to get started because I know I will improve and learn, which is always my main priority. My job now is to train hard, get to know the players and staff and do everything I can to reach my best level."

‌



Cristian Romero nears Tottenham exit as transfer fee agreed amid Arsenal interest READ MORE :

It is a second spell for Rulli at City, having previously spent the 2016-17 season at the club without making an appearance.

Football Director Hugo Viana said “It’s a pleasure to welcome Gerónimo back to the Club. The experience he brings is obvious – he has played at the very highest level for many years.

“I have been really impressed by him during our conversations, a strong desire to join us. It’s clear we are getting a brilliant professional, as well as a top ‘keeper.

Article continues below

“Everyone at City is looking forward to welcoming him back to the Club. The qualities he will bring are ones we need, and together with Gigio and Marcus make a great team. Our goalkeeper coaches are really happy with the group.”

Sports.title: Netherlands make shock move for ex-Premier League boss after Arne Slot snub
Sports.content:
Netherlands make shock move for ex-Premier League boss after Arne Slot snub

The Netherlands are looking for a new manager after parting company with Ronald Koeman and have found a new contender for the role following failed talks with Arne Slot

View 2 Images Arne Slot walked away from the Netherlands job

Roberto Martinez is in talks to become the next manager of the Netherlands, a month after leaving his role with Portugal. Martinez left Portugal after they were knocked out of the World Cup by Spain in the last 16 - but could be set for a swift return to international management.

‌



The Netherlands parted company with Ronald Koeman after they were knocked out of the World Cup in the last 32 by Morocco in June. The penalty shoot-out exit was a painful way to end the tournament and Koeman stepped down from his second spell in charge.

‌



Arne Slot had appeared heavy favourite to succeed Koeman following his departure from Liverpool at the end of last season. But talks with the KNVB (Royal Dutch Football Association) did not lead to a contract offer.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Cristiano Ronaldo marries Georgina Rodriguez as football icon shares ring picture READ MORE :

Tottenham hold the key to Arsenal transfer after Mikel Arteta changes target READ MORE :

Slot has since explained that he withdrew from the process due to his desire to stay in club football. De Telegraaf now reports that Martinez is in the frame to take over the side.

The 53-year-old started out in club management, with stints at Swansea, Wigan and Everton, but has spent the past decade in international football. He spent six years with Belgium before joining Portugal in 2023.

‌



Martinez led Belgium to third place at the 2018 World Cup and No.1 in the FIFA world rankings, but left after being knocked out in the group stages of the 2022 World Cup. He won the Nations League with Portugal last year before this summer's disappointment in North America.

View 2 Images Roberto Martinez is available after leaving Portugal (Image: Zhizhao Wu/Getty Images)

Despite being criticised for his conservative playing style, it seems he is the KNVB's second choice for the Netherlands gig after Slot ruled himself out.

‌



"Over the past few weeks, and particularly the past few days, various reports have appeared regarding the vacancy at the Dutch national team, suggesting that I had withdrawn from the process after lengthy negotiations, including regarding salary and contract duration," the former Liverpool boss told Voetbal International.

“That speculation is incorrect. We simply never reached that stage of the talks. At this stage of my career, I prefer to see myself on the training pitch with my players every day. Something that is simply not possible in the same way with a national team.

“And (this is) why I chose not to continue the talks and not to start negotiations on what a possible contract might look like. I have enormous respect for the national team and for the KNVB and can only be positive about the professional manner in which the talks proceeded that week.

Article continues below

“For now, I believe that club football still has a lot to offer me. It would be a great honour to represent my country as national coach one day. However, this was not the right moment for me.”

Sports.title: Fery feels 'no added pressure' despite being British No 1 as he returns
Sports.content:
Arthur Fery insists he feels “no added pressure” as the new British No 1 prepares to return to action this weekend for the first time since his memorable run to the Wimbledon semi-finals.

Fery became only the fifth British player to make the last four of the men's singles at Wimbledon in the Open era and has surged into the top 40 in the ATP rankings, have been ended 2025 in 198th.

The 23-year-old skipped the Canadian Open to ensure he is rested but will be back this weekend at the ATP 1000 event in Cincinnati, live on Sky Sports Tennis.

"It's obviously a privilege to be to No 1 in in Britain. I'm not gonna put any added pressure on myself," Fery told Sky Sports.

"I'm just going to take every match as it comes, keep working hard day in, day out, both in practice and at tournaments, and see where that takes me. That's what I've been doing this year and it's worked well so far, so I'm just going to keep going in the same direction."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Arthur Fery says it was 'incredible' to reach the Wimbledon semi-finals and vows to keep the British No 1 spot

Fery will look to ensure he is seeded at the last Grand Slam of the year, the US Open, which begins on August 30, by having a strong run in Cincinnati.

He has been training in London since Wimbledon but flew to Ohio earlier this week to acclimatise to the conditions, with Fery also saying fellow players have been welcoming as he adjusts to his sudden rise.

"All the way through the fortnight, it was just incredible to have so much support. I'd never had that amount of people and fans behind me, so that was really special," he said.

"Now here in in Cincinnati, playing my second Masters 1000 main draw, I'm really looking forward to playing all these tough events this year."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky's Jacquie Beltrao looks ahead to a bright future for Arthur Fery after his semi-final exit to Alexander Zverev at Wimbledon

Draper could meet Djokovic in Cincinnati

Jack Draper has been given a wild card for the Cincinnati Open and could meet Novak Djokovic in the third round of the tournament.

Draper will play rising Spanish star Martin Landeluce in the first round before facing Italy's Matteo Arnaldi. Should Draper win those two matches, he could meet Djokovic next week.

However, the 24-year-old will likely simply hope he is fit for multiple matches after he was in tears during his defeat last week to Terence Atmane in the first round of the Canadian Open. It was unclear whether that was related to his recent arm injury recurring.

Cameron Norrie will face Croatia's Dino Prizmic while Jan Choinski goes up against Argentina's Thiago Agustin Tirante and Fery has a bye to the second round since he is seeded.

Katie Boulter is the only Brit in the women's draw and she will play USA's Katie Volynets.

Sports.title: Tielemans: I did not expect to leave Aston Villa for Man Utd this summer
Sports.content:
'Not really, no' - the perhaps surprising answer from Manchester United’s summer signing Youri Tielemans when asked whether he expected to leave his former club Aston Villa in this window.

It is easy to forget Man Utd swiftly and covertly signed a player with eight years of Premier League experience at what feels like the height of his footballing powers due to a generous release clause of just £35m.

In his first interview since joining the club, Tielemans has opened up about just how the move came around, especially having been of interest to Manchester United on a few occasions in the past as well.

"There has been two times that I spoke with the club, but it did not achieve anything so I was just very calm about it," Tielemans said.

"It was mainly my agent that was dealing with it, I was more so focused on the World Cup which was a big thing for me. When it was time that it was accepted and acceptable, I would say then I was made aware.

Image: Tielemans signed a five-year deal with Man Utd

"I was not expecting much [a summer move], to be fair. I was just focused on my football, focused on the World Cup, trying to perform as best as I could for my country. Then every summer something can happen."

Tielemans joined Villa as a free agent after leaving Leicester when they were relegated to the Championship. For some reason, a move to the conventional 'top six' never seemed rumoured or close during his time at either of his previous clubs - which is why his move to Manchester United was deemed a surprise.

But did he think the opportunity had passed him by? "Not really, because I know that at Villa we did amazing things," Tielemans explained.

Image: Tielemans made his first appearance for Man Utd against PSG

"We achieved the Europa League win which was great for the club but there are still clubs above Aston Villa, and Manchester United is one of them.

"Especially at this moment, there is a very positive mood in and around the club so I am just hopeful that we can have a great story together.

"Aston Villa is a great club and I owe them the world. They have put me back at my best level so I am very thankful."

Reuniting with Evans and Rashford

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo were among more Manchester United players returning for pre-season training.

Although Tielemans is still getting used to his new surroundings, he will have felt at ease knowing one member of staff very well in particular - Jonny Evans.

The former centre-back spent four and a half years with Tielemans at Leicester and is now a key member of Michael Carrick's backroom staff.

When I asked just how nice it felt to be reunited with his former team-mate, he couldn't resist a huge smile.

Image: Jonny Evans played with Tielemans at Leicester, and is now a coach at Man Utd

"Jonny has always been a main character," Tielemans said. "He has always been trying to educate young players and he welcomed me at Leicester and now here.

"It is a bit weird to see him as a staff member to be honest, but it is going great and he knows me, he knows what I need and what I can bring to the team so it helps me as well."

Another relatively new team-mate Tielemans spent slightly less time with was Marcus Rashford. The pair spent six months together when the England international was on loan at Aston Villa for the second half of the 2024/25 season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player With Marcus Rashford being fully reintegrated into the Manchester United squad after his loan at Barcelona came to an end earlier this summer, Sky Sports News' Danyal Khan explains how the England forward's return can benefit the club.

There is a lot of attention on the Man Utd winger's return to the club as well as what he can offer this team, Tielemans only has fond memories of their time at Villa Park together and is looking forward to more of them.

He said: "He was great. There had been so much talk about him and bringing pressure with the media around him, but I thought he was just so good.

"He was very humble, he was hard working and from the first training session, you could tell, his touch, his acceleration was amazing.

"That was just what we needed at the time at Villa as well so he did many good things and hopefully he can bring them here."

World Cup, his injury and Balogun's red card reversal

Image: Tielemans was Belgium's captain at the 2026 World Cup

Tielemans has had an eventful summer, even before his surprise move to Manchester United.

He captained Belgium at this summer's World Cup, who were knocked out in the quarter-finals by eventual winners Spain. Tielemans was unable to play in the quarter-final after picking up an injury in the warm-up, but for any Man Utd fans concerned whether he has any lingering injury concerns, he is more than ready for the new season.

Tielemans said: "It was just an overload of too many games, too many minutes and unfortunately my body could not cope with it anymore.

"We played 120 minutes against Senegal and from there, we had less time in between games. We played the USA three or four days later, then three days after that, we played against Spain. In the warm-up, my body switched off for some reason."

Before his injury, the midfielder played a key role in Belgium's World Cup campaign, scoring two goals in their dramatic win against Senegal in the round of 32.

Image: Belgium beat the USA 4-1 despite the controversy surrounding Folarin Balogun's suspended red card

However, perhaps the most eventful game was their round of 16 tie against the USA. In what proved to be one of the most controversial decisions of the tournament, USA striker Folarin Balogun's red card was suspended for the tie, although in the end it did not matter as Belgium went on to win 4-1.

"Originally we were surprised by the decision to revert the red card and his suspension," Tielemans said.

"Now for us, it did not really change anything other than the preparation leading up to the game because it is a different type of player than the other player that was meant to play.

"Other than that, we were very calm and we just accepted our fate and tried to have a good game."

Sports.title: What next for Birmingham City? Why Davies is changing his approach
Sports.content:
Birmingham City is a football club transformed. Over 20,000 season tickets have been sold for the forthcoming Championship season, with 14,000 more on the waiting list. Fan parks surround St Andrew's these days. The buzz around the place is palpable.

There are grand plans to reconnect England's second city to the club that bears its name, unlocking its true potential. Supporters clubs are springing up around the world, a product of Tom Brady's presence. And all the talk is of trying to be Premier League ready.

Given this context, with an ambitious ownership and a success-starved support, it is understandable if Birmingham are in a hurry. Excitement brings expectation, not just internally but externally. There is the sense of a club going places. But it takes time.

On reflection, maybe last season was a moment for the club to breathe rather than a case of lost momentum. After all, you must go back 14 years to the 2011/12 season, when Birmingham were in Europe, for a better finish than the 10th-place effort of 2025/26.

"It was our first season back, which people found hard to remember at times," Birmingham manager Chris Davies tells Sky Sports. He is not talking about the club's supporters - "they have been great" - but everyone. This is a man carrying a lot of hopes and dreams.

"One thing I did learn was that I can handle it," he says. "I can handle the ups and downs." There had not been too many of the latter as Birmingham won the League One title with a record-breaking 111 points, their possession football proving utterly dominant.

Last season was more testing. "You can know about the Championship but to feel it is something different." England's second tier asked different questions. Davies and his team did not always have the answers. Plan A worked only some of the time.

"We came up from League One playing total football, having 80 per cent possession with a lot of circulating the ball, a lot of dominating the ball. It was really effective for us because we just controlled games pretty much the whole way through," he explains.

"In the Championship we were very technical in our recruitment of some smaller players, more technical players, and we tried to use that style. It had really good days and it had days where we just didn't have enough punch, especially away from home."

In that context, opening the season with a hard-fought Carabao Cup win at Swansea in which Birmingham scored the only goal having had 39 per cent of the ball was more than just satisfying. It suggested that his Blues side have added different elements to their game.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Carabao Cup first-round match between Swansea and Birmingham

The scorer, August Priske, is a robust young target-man added in January who looks to have benefited from that half-season in the Championship. The 22-year-old Dane also netted the opening goal against Barcelona in front of a packed St Andrew's last month.

"Jhon Solis, Carlos Vicente and August came in at the same time and that little six months that they did have is their initiation to what English football is like, what the Championship is like, and now they are ready to go. They have all done very well."

Vicente, a combative Spanish winger, provided the assist for Priske's goal at Swansea. Solis also scored against Barcelona with the Colombian already proving a popular figure with the fans. He adds presence to Birmingham's midfield just as Priske does up top.

"When I reflected on the season, I thought for us to take the next step and progress, physicality is going to be really important. The game now is a lot of man-to-man pressing, a lot of set-piece emphasis. You need the physical capacity to deal with it."

That thinking has shaped Birmingham's summer too. Supplementing those winter additions, the club have brought in Dael Fry. The expectation is that a 6ft 4in centre-back with nearly 300 Championship appearances to his name will be able to adapt quickly.

The intention is to add to what Davies has already built, rather than pivot completely. "As a team that can keep the ball, it is a lot easier to then move into a more pragmatic or direct style than being a team that only knows how to play pragmatic or direct football."

That change actually began during the closing weeks of the last campaign. Birmingham were in 17th place in mid-April, but Davies used the brief international break in the spring to make some of these adjustments to their style of play. They went more direct.

Image: Christoph Klarer's passing sonar shows how Birmingham have become more direct

"I started thinking about being a little bit more flexible with the shape we were using and how we were positioning ourselves, but focusing more on more direct play, more transitions and more set-pieces if possible. So we sort of finished the season that way."

Birmingham ended the campaign on a five-game unbeaten run, earning that top-10 finish and taking some belief into the summer.

"It is a fine balance because we don't want to lose what we're good at. What I won't come away from is the pressing. I don't think any team last season in the Championship really played through our press consistently. I thought it was really effective for us."

But there will be tweaks once Birmingham win the ball back. "I think that hopefully is something that we can have as a weapon that we can use a little bit more. When we get the ball, just to go forward that little bit quicker, hopefully win more set-pieces."

That explains another addition behind the scenes. Birmingham have brought in a specialist set-piece coach in Scott Fry, with Davies identifying dead-ball situations as an obvious way that his team can become genuine promotion contenders this season.

Solis scored from one against Barcelona. Priske's winner against Swansea came after a set-piece found Vicente and he squared the ball for the striker. In other words, this emphasis on set-pieces is already making the difference. And Davies has been doing his sums.

"We have a set-piece coach and the idea is to score more from them. We needed to score 70-odd goals really to be in among those top teams last season." Crucially, that was the total hit by the top six but not the rest of the Championship. Birmingham scored 57.

The task this time around is to find those extra 13 goals somehow. "If six or seven of those can come from set-pieces and two or three can come from counter-attacks, then you only need another two or three from your general football. So it is absolutely doable."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jude Bellingham discusses his love of Birmingham and his love of cricket

Absolutely doable. That sums up the mood. Last time, they were learning about the Championship. Now they know. "It was not just me, several players had never played in it before. Now they have 40 games in the bank. They know what it is like away at Millwall."

At the training ground, Davies has tried to strip back the buzzwords that once adorned the walls. No more gimmicks is the mantra now. Leaner and meaner, like the squad. The feeling is that there is more continuity now, that this Birmingham are ready to kick on.

Craig Gardner has left as director of football but the club has played down the impact, leaning on the experienced Mike Rigg. Commercially, Birmingham continue to grow, with the biggest revenue of any Championship club not reliant on parachute money.

After storming up and then stabilising, the next step awaits Birmingham City. And now, it feels like everyone is ready for it. "I am confident that we can keep progressing. That is the big thing," says Davies. "We just need to keep moving forward and getting stronger."

Sports.title: Championship play-off changes, new managers & star players - the EFL is BACK!
Sports.content:
The 2026/27 EFL season is here!

We kick off on Friday night with Wolves vs Blackburn Rovers, and every Championship, League One and League Two game is LIVE this weekend!

But what have we got in store for the new campaign? We take a look at some of the key stories...

Championship

From top six to top eight... a new play-off system has arrived!

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Simeon Gholam explains all you need to know on how the play-offs have changed this season in the Championship

The most significant alteration to domestic football in decades has happened over the summer, with the Championship play-offs expanding from a top-six spot to a top-eight position this season, presenting clubs with more opportunity for promotion.

What has (and hasn't) changed?

1st and 2nd are automatically promoted as normal.

3rd and 4th still qualify for the semi-finals.

5th vs 8th and 6th vs 7th in one-off eliminator ties at the home of the side who finishes higher up the league.

The winners of the eliminator ties progress to the semi-finals, to face 3rd and 4th in two-legged ties with the second leg at the home of the side that finishes higher up the league.

One other key thing to note is that, whatever happens, 3rd will face the lowest-ranked team remaining in the semi-finals. So if 8th beats 5th, and 6th beats 7th in the eliminators, 3rd will face 8th and 4th will face 6th. There is no pre-set path for the semi-finals before the eliminators.

in the semi-finals. So if 8th beats 5th, and 6th beats 7th in the eliminators, 3rd will face 8th and 4th will face 6th. There is no pre-set path for the semi-finals before the eliminators. As per usual, the winners of the two semi-finals meet at Wembley for a place in the Premier League.

Are the relegated clubs automatic favourites?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kevin Nolan and Darren Moore tell the EFL Show why Jarrod Bowen is key for West Ham's hopes for an instant return to the Premier League

It did not take long for West Ham and Wolves to be installed as favourites for an immediate return to the Premier League.

The Hammers are playing at this level for the first time in 14 years, and have kept hold of head coach Nuno Espirito Santo and key asset Jarrod Bowen.

Both are familiar with this level. Nuno won the Championship - with Wolves - in 2018, while Bowen played in it with Hull City before he left for east London.

Wolves, meanwhile, replaced boss Rob Edwards with the relatively unknown quantity of Cesar Peixoto in the summer. But the quality in their squad could prove telling, with Andre, Mateus Mane, Santiago Bueno and Hugo Bueno sticking about.

They have also added Raul Jimenez and Kieran Trippier to the bank. Experience and class.

It is Burnley where a bit more uncertainty lingers. They have appointed a new head coach in Nicky Hayen, a 45-year-old Belgian who has previously managed Club Brugge and Genk.

But it is worth remembering the Clarets have won promotion in their last two Championship seasons - both times with 100+ points. They are experts at this level.

According to the Sky Sports supercomputer, West Ham and Wolves are the two favourites, with Burnley in fourth just behind Middlesbrough...

Middlesbrough go big to try and get over the line

It was some campaign for Middlesbrough last season. They spent more days in the top two than any other club, but managed to finish fifth.

They were then the victim of the Spygate saga, lost to Southampton in the play-off semi-finals, were reinstated to the final, then lost at Wembley to a stoppage-time Oli McBurnie goal for Hull City.

But any potential hangover looks like it has already been left behind with some of their work in the transfer window.

Owner Steve Gibson has taken his chequebook out and spent serious money to strengthen. Striker Will Lankshear has already made his mark with the winning goal against Wrexham in the Carabao Cup. He scored 11 goals for a struggling Oxford side last season and arrives from Spurs.

Sebastian Berhalter comes in, having last been seen playing for the USA at the World Cup, while goalkeeper Radek Vitek from Manchester United is also an eye-catching addition. He impressed on loan at Bristol City last season.

Kim Hellberg and some Boro fans may be wondering where this backing was in January when they were crying out for reinforcements, but it has certainly led to a swell of excitement at the Riverside about what's possible this season.

Can Southampton escape Spygate scandal?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking exclusively to Sky Sports' Mark McAdam before the FA charge, Southampton boss Tonda Eckert revealed the challenges he has faced after the Spygate scandal that resulted in their expulsion from the Championship play-offs

It was the story that dominated the landscape of last season. A shockwave went around the footballing world when Southampton were expelled from the play-offs after their role in the Spygate scandal.

But the club were quick to back Tonda Eckert, and although an FA charge still hangs over the boss, they have tried to move on and heal the wounds caused by the damage.

Fears of a player exodus have been quelled, with only midfielder Shea Charles departing so far, and the club has brought in goalkeeper Daniel Peretz and striker Cyle Larin permanently, after both starred on loan in the second half of last season.

They will have to overcome a four-point deduction. But they came from a long way back last season with a remarkable run in the second half of the campaign, and they certainly have the quality to challenge.

Managerial changes in the Championship

There are also a few other managerial changes to make a note of. Tony Mowbray is back at Blackburn Rovers four years after he left the club, while Watford have brought in Alessio Dionisi.

Elsewhere, Michael Skubala left Lincoln City after leading them to promotion to join Bristol City. While his exit opened the door for the Imps to make the unique move of appointing joint-managers in the role. Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw take the reins at Sincil Bank.

League One

Will Leicester turn things around?

Image: Leicester City manager Russell Martin

For just the second time in their history, and just 10 years after they won the Premier League title, Leicester City have found themselves in League One.

Russell Martin has taken the helm, as they look to end a miserable run of back-to-back relegations. He also has work to do in winning over some doubters, after miserable ends to his spells at Southampton and Rangers in his last two roles.

The addition of experience has been the aim of the summer, with the likes of Liam Cullen, Conor Chaplin and Wes Burns already joining.

A new dawn for Wednesday and who else could compete for promotion?

The Chansiri era is finally over at Sheffield Wednesday, and there has been a swirl of optimism around the club under new owner David Storch, despite relegation.

Henrik Pedersen, who led the Owls through the grim 2025/26 season, has been given the opportunity to see if he can get more out of a squad that is actually built to compete.

Louie Barry is an eye-catching addition. Injuries have blighted his progress but he has shown what a star he can be at this level for Stockport County, while Barry Bannan is back home after his stint at Millwall.

Luton are quite fancied under Jack Wilshere after a positive run in the second half of last season.

As are Plymouth Argyle, who have been exceptional so far in 2026, just missing out on the play-offs.

Managerial changes in League One

Image: Aaron Ramsey has taken his first permanent managerial role at Oxford United

There has been a particularly notable appointment at Oxford United, with Aaron Ramsey taking his first permanent managerial role to replace Matt Bloomfield, who surprisingly departed in the summer.

It has not been an easy start for Ramsey, however, as he has already had to deal with a transfer embargo which has left him unable to make any additions at the relegated club.

Elsewhere, Daniel Stendel has returned to Barnsley, Martin Drury has taken charge at Huddersfield Town and Jimmy McNulty left Rochdale to join Stockport following the departure of Dave Challinor.

Bromley's first season in the third tier!

Bromley were promoted to the EFL for the first time in their history in 2024, and it took just two seasons for them to seal promotion from League Two.

The Ravens won the title last season, and will now compete in the third tier of English football for the first time. It has only been 11 years since they were promoted to the National League for the first time.

They have been installed as the favourites for relegation, but Andy Woodman's side have defied the critics before and will be keen to do so again. Don't rule out anything at Hayes Lane.

League Two

All change at York and Rochdale

Image: Scott Lindsey has been appointed at York City

After 10 years away, York City are back in the EFL!

But it has not been all smooth sailing since. A couple of weeks before the start of the season, manager Stuart Maynard - who led them to promotion with more than 100 points - departed the club.

His replacement Scott Lindsey has not proven popular so far. In his first game in charge York exited the Carabao Cup at the preliminary phase, with fans booing and calling for the return of Maynard.

Not quite the return the Minstermen would have wanted to League Two.

The side they edged to automatic promotion in the National League, Rochdale, have also lost their manager after fighting their way through the play-offs.

McNulty moved on to Stockport, and they have dipped into non-League to appoint their new manager, with Ian Watson joining from National League North side South Shields.

Will Salford City finally get over the line?

Image: Macaulay Langstaff is one of the summer arrivals at Salford City

It is seven years now since Salford City were promoted to League Two, and still they have not managed to get over the line.

Last season was the closest they have come, losing in the play-off final to Notts County. Manager Karl Robinson has since departed, with Peter Cklamovski taking his place, having most recently been in charge of the Malaysia national side.

They have gone big in the transfer market, too. Macaulay Langstaff and Luke Molyneux have already arrived. Could this be the year the club owned by Gary Neville and David Beckham finally reach League One?

Managerial changes in League Two

Elsewhere, there are a lot of new managers to keep an eye on. Chris Hogg has come in at Northampton Town, while another relegated club in Rotherham United have appointed Alex Bruce.

Darrell Clarke takes charge at Tranmere Rovers, Lee Grant is at Walsall and Hayden Mullins will lead Newport County this season.
