Madbouly said the initiative had also created significant employment opportunities, noting that the unemployment rate had fallen below 6 percent. “We are moving in the right direction despite all the unprecedented challenges we are facing,” he said.

The prime minister also highlighted the “Ras El Hekma” medical project in Matrouh, which has been fully developed, as well as expansion plans across the governorate. He pointed to the construction of an entirely new building for Alamein Hospital and the “Alam El Roum” Hospital, the governorate’s main hospital, which has hundreds of beds.

He added that major medical services are being implemented alongside housing and development projects, as well as the Alam El Roum project being developed through an Egyptian-Qatari partnership.

Madbouly stressed that tourism is a genuine source of income for Egypt, saying it is encouraging to see the large presence of foreign tourists on the North Coast. This, he noted, means an inflow of foreign currency into the country, as well as job opportunities for young people living in these areas throughout the year.

He noted that the North Coast has strong tourism potential, pointing to the acceleration in the development of tourism projects. Such projects, he said, will create job opportunities and generate billions of dollars in revenues for the state.

The prime minister also touched on the high-speed railway serving the development process, saying it would help citizens travel from Cairo to Matrouh, as well as along the “Ain Sokhna-Matrouh-Salloum” route, alongside electricity, energy and development projects.

He stressed that the government is safeguarding the state’s rights and that an integrated vision for the development of the North Coast will benefit the people of Matrouh by generating jobs and development opportunities.

Madbouly affirmed that development is at the heart of every part of Egypt, urging people to consider the scale of development achieved over the past 12 years, compared with the situation in Egypt before that period and the country’s current position, despite the unprecedented external challenges.

He added that the government is focusing on improving citizens’ quality of life and has comprehensive plans to address existing challenges. The government is nearing completion of a program aimed at launching an economic transformation over the next three years.

“Our goal is to anticipate all possible scenarios that could unfold globally and their impact on us, including the continuation of the conflicts currently taking place,” he said.

On the energy sector, Madbouly said the government reviews the file on a weekly basis with the officials responsible for it.

He added that, under the visions and strategies set by the political leadership for the sector since 2014, the state has undertaken a large number of projects whose benefits are now being realized and whose returns are being reaped during the current phase.

He affirmed that Egypt is capable of meeting the energy sector’s needs over the coming period.

World.title: Finance Minister: LE 6 bln targeted for cash payment of third tranche of exporters’ dues
World.content:
Finance Minister Ahmed Kouchouk said the government is targeting the allocation of six billion LE to pay in cash the third tranche of overdue dues owed to exporters for shipments made before July 1, 2024.

Kouchouk said applications from exporting companies seeking to benefit from the third tranche of the cash payment initiative will be accepted from Aug. 16 through Oct. 1, with payments scheduled to be disbursed on Oct. 22.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, August 11, 2026, the minister said more than LE 80 billion has been paid to exporters over the past six years, adding that the government aims to clear all outstanding dues within two years.

He noted that LE 48 billion has been allocated in the current budget to accelerate the provision of export support, while export subsidies reached LE 28 billion in fiscal year 2025/2026, marking annual growth of 55%.

Kouchouk said there is ongoing coordination and integration with the Ministry of Investment and Foreign Trade to develop the export system and boost the export sector.

He stressed that the government is working to provide exporters with liquidity to support the growth and competitiveness of Egypt’s goods and services exports, adding that it aims to significantly increase annual allocations for export support and promotion in order to open new markets for Egyptian products.

Meanwhile, Nevine Mansour, the minister’s adviser for economic institutions’ relations, said LE 12.6 billion in cash had been paid to around 2,500 exporting companies during the last fiscal year.

She noted that the amount represented the total value of the first and second tranches of overdue dues paid in cash during fiscal year 2025/2026, instead of being paid over two fiscal years.

World.title: Petroleum Minister: Proactive plans remain in place to secure natural gas market needs
World.content:
Minister of Petroleum and Mineral Resources Karim Badawi has affirmed that the petroleum sector continues to implement comprehensive, proactive plans to secure the local market’s natural gas needs.

He stressed the importance of managing shifts in consumption with high efficiency and flexibility, while maintaining maximum readiness to handle any emergencies or developments.

This came as the minister reviewed the operational status of the national natural gas grid directly from the Egyptian Natural Gas Company (GASCO) control center.

He inspected the steady flow of gas to various domestic sectors and evaluated strategic plans to meet energy demands through the remainder of the summer season.

During his visit, the minister verified uninterrupted gas supplies to power generation plants to ensure grid stability amid soaring temperatures.

He also monitored deliveries to the industrial sector to guarantee that factories operate at full capacity, alongside fulfilling domestic market requirements and export commitments.

Badawi noted that decisive state measures, backed by the political leadership and the government, have successfully met local demand throughout the first half of the summer.

Key actions included procuring regasification vessels and natural gas shipments, boosting domestic production, and implementing forward-looking supply strategies, he said.

Concluding his remarks, the minister underscored the necessity of continuous coordination between the petroleum and electricity sectors, alongside other relevant authorities.

This integrated approach aims to guarantee sustainable energy supplies for all state sectors moving forward, supported by real-time monitoring of the grid, consumption rates, and supply flows.

World.title: Chipolopolo’s Musonda joins Zesco Utd
World.content:
Chipolopolo striker Kennedy Musonda has returned to the Zambia Super League, signing for Super Division side Zesco United after a three-year stint abroad.

Zesco officially announced Musonda’s acquisition on 12 August 2026 as part of its signings ahead of the 2026 Transitional League.

“ZESCO United Football Club is delighted to announce the acquisition of new players ahead of the Transition League. Kennedy Musonda returns to the Zambia Super League. At Young Africans he scored 32 goals and won 3 Tanzanian Premier League titles, 3 Cups, 2 Community Shields, and reached the CAF Confederation Cup Final,” the club stated.

Musonda spent two and a half years at Tanzanian giants Young Africans after leaving Power Dynamos.

During his final season with Power in 2022/2023, he helped the Kitwe side win the Super Division title with 11 goals.

After his contract with Yanga expired, the striker moved to Israel a year ago, joining second-tier side Hapoel Ramat Gan Givatayim.

He was linked with a return to Power Dynamos before opting for Zesco.

On the international stage, Musonda scored 4 goals for Chipolopolo during the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers.

Musonda is not the only new arrival at the Ndola club as Zesco have also bolstered its squad with more additions.

The club has also bolstered its squad with goalkeeper Patrick Chooma from Leopards FC, Chadian midfielder Yves Allarabaye from Foullah Edifice, Gilbert Tetani from Mufulira Wanderers, and John Mulenga who joins from Green Buffaloes having featured for Young Green Buffaloes.

The signing of Musonda is expected to add firepower as Zesco prepare for both domestic and continental assignments in the Transitional League.

ZESCO’S NEW SIGNEES

Brice Sindjo – Cameroonian forward from Colombe Sportive

Happy Nsiku – Defender from Red Arrows

Antony Shipanuka – Winger from Red Arrows

Patrick Chooma – Goalkeeper from Leopards FC

Yves Allarabaye – Chadian midfielder from Foullah Edifice

Gilbert Tetani – From Mufulira Wanderers

John Mulenga – From Green Buffaloes

World.title: Police officers directed to be professional -Musamba
World.content:
Inspector General of Police, Graphel Musamba, has directed all police officers to discharge their duties with professionalism, integrity, neutrality and respect for the constitution, ahead of the August polls.

In a statement issued to the media, Mr Musamba, says the Police have enhanced crime detection operations and Rapid Response Teams across all provinces, in a bid to ensure that every eligible citizen can vote freely and peacefully, without intimidation.

Mr Musamba further directed the police officers to exercise respect for human rights while dealing with criminal conduct, protect every citizen equally and arrest all individuals who commit crime, regardless of political affiliation.

He said that the Police and Electoral Commission of Zambia have coordinated measures to safeguard electoral materials, polling stations, election officials and integrity of the electoral process.

“Every voter, every candidate and every election official will be protected without fear, favour or political consideration,” said Mr Musamba.

Mr Musamba said that the Zambia police service has progressively implemented its 2026 electoral security plan with additional police officers deployed across the country to strengthen police visibility, improve response times and reassure communities.

Mr Musamba also urged members of the public to play a part in safeguarding peace by returning home, to work or continue with lawful activities after casting their votes and avoid loitering around polling stations, unless as accredited by the ECZ.

He also urged members of the public to obtain election results only from official and authorised sources and to avoid circulating or relying on unverified information, rumours and speculative announcements on social media.

Mr Musamba further urged the public to expect increased police presence and snap security checkpoints on selected roads, as a preventive measure that is intended to enhance public safety.

World.title: Poll staff deployed-Kanchibiya
World.content:
The Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) has commenced the deployment of poll staff in Kanchibiya District ahead of this week’s general elections.

Kanchibiya District Electoral Officer (DEO) Augustine Chanda says the deployment follows briefings conducted for various stakeholders, including uniformed personnel, the media, Non-governmental Organisations (NGOs) and faith-based organisations.

He said the commission also conducted briefings for poll staff in preparation for their deployment to various polling stations across the district.

Mr Chanda said the deployment exercise will begin with staff assigned to the furthest areas, including Cheweshimfwamba to ensure that all personnel are in their respective areas before polling day.

He expressed hope that the deployment of all poll staff in the district will be completed by midday tomorrow.

And Mr Chanda has said that poll staff were also taking oaths of affirmation as part of the requirements for their engagement with the ECZ and the electoral process.

He urged all stakeholders who had been briefed by the commission to participate in the electoral process in accordance with established guidelines.

Mr Chanda said the guidelines and stakeholder engagements were aimed at ensuring effective coordination of operations among all players during the elections.

He also challenged the media to disseminate accurate information to members of the public who may not have an opportunity to witness activities taking place at various polling stations.

He added that police are expected to maintain peace and protect voters.

And Mr Chanda said the commission’s priority was to maintain voter confidence and ensure that the electoral process was free, fair and inclusive to all eligible citizens.

World.title: Liato family thanks President Hakainde Hichilema
World.content:
Family of the late former Cabinet Minister, Austin Liato, has expressed profound gratitude to President Hakainde Hichilema, for having accorded Mr Liato a National Mourning.

Family representative, Jonathan Liato, also thanked the church, political leaders, friends and members of the public for standing with them during the period of National Mourning.

speaking during the burial ceremony at Leopards Hill Memorial Park today, Mr Liato said the support and presence of mourners demonstrated the love and respect that people had for the late Mr Liato.

He said the family was particularly humbled by the presence of the President of the Republic of Zambia, through his representative, saying it was a demonstration of solidarity with the family during its time of grief.

Mr Liato also thanked serving and former Members of Parliament, ministers, civic and government leaders for standing with the family and honouring the life and service of the late Mr Liato.

He further expressed gratitude to church leaders and men and women of God for their prayers, words of comfort and for giving the bereaved family hope through the Christian message of resurrection.

Mr Liato also commended the church, service family, friends, choir, organisers and all those who assisted the family from the time of the late Liato’s death, saying their support helped ensure that the funeral proceedings were conducted with dignity and care.

He said Mr Liato lived a life dedicated to God and the people of Zambia, adding that the family would continue to remember and honour the late Mr Liato for his service to the nation and the people.

World.title: President Hichilema speaks infrastructure development in Matero
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema has assured residents of Matero and Lima constituencies of more infrastructure development if voted for the second term of office, in the August 13 general elections.

Speaking when he addressed multitudes of Matero and Lima residents at Chunga grounds, President Hichilema committed to work on township roads in both constituencies, saying he wants all the township roads to be upgraded to bituminous standard.

He indicated that most of the township roads in Matero and Lima constituencies are in a deplorable state.

And President Hichilema further assured the people in the two constituencies of improved water supply once voted back into office, in the August 13 polls.

The Head of State said he was aware that water supply was a challenge in the two constituencies, pledging to work on the drainage system in Matero and Lima, noting that during the rainy season the said areas often experience floods.

President Hichilema said the improved drainage system will allow water to flow freely without causing flooding.

Meanwhile, President Hichilema has promised to build additional health facilities in the newly created Lima constituency.

The President said his goal is to ensure that women give birth in a safe facility.

President Hichilema also announced at the same community engagement that skills training centres for the youths will be constructed in Matero and Lima constituencies.

The President has since urged the people of Matero and Lima constituencies to also vote for the UPND candidates in the forthcoming general elections, saying voting for UPND candidates who include Councillors and Members of Parliament will enable him to easily deliver development.

World.title: Nakonde ballot papers verified
World.content:
The Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) in Nakonde District, in Muchinga Province has completed the verification of ballot papers ahead of Thursday’s general elections.

The verification exercise was conducted in the presence of stakeholders and representatives from the United Party for National Development (UPND) and the National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity (NRPUP).

Nakonde District Electoral Officer Donald Mwanza says that ballot papers from Nsonde and Mukumbe polling stations, drawn from 2 wards under 2 constituencies, were sampled during the exercise.

He stated that the stakeholders expressed satisfaction with the process and confirmed that everything was in order.

Mr Mwanza further disclosed that the dispatch of polling officials to hard-to-reach areas has commenced today.

He said 10 polling stations will receive officials and election materials in this first phase of the dispatch.

The District Electoral Officer added that both transport and personnel are ready and that the district is fully set for the poll scheduled for Thursday, August 13th, 2026.

World.title: ECZ conducts ballot verification in Mpika
World.content:
The Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) in Mpika says it remains committed to ensuring transparency, credibility and fairness in the electoral process ahead of tomorrow’s General Elections.

The Commission made the assurance following a ballot paper verification exercise conducted at the Mpika Town Council Chambers in Mpika District in Muchinga Province.

The exercise was witnessed by various election stakeholders who participated in the verification process.

Mpika District Electoral Officer Samuel Musenga said the verification exercise was necessary and conducted in accordance with Zambia’s electoral processes and procedures.

Mr Musenga said the exercise was important as it helped to dispel any doubts among stakeholders ahead of the general elections.

He expressed satisfaction with the active participation of stakeholders in the exercise, saying their involvement was key to promoting transparency, accountability and credibility in the electoral process.

Mr Musenga further disclosed that the deployment of poll staff had commenced in Mpika District and that all poll staff would be fully deployed by today.

He said the ECZ was working tirelessly to ensure that all logistical arrangements were completed ahead of polling day.

Meanwhile, stakeholders have expressed satisfaction with the ballot paper verification exercise conducted in Mpika District.

Mpika District Southern Africa Centre for the Constructive Resolution of Disputes (SACCORD) Coordinator Tresfold Chifwalo said the verification exercise was conducted smoothly without any problems.

Mr Chifwalo said the exercise had given stakeholders confidence in the credibility of the forthcoming elections.

“ECZ must continue engaging all stakeholders as it promotes the true meaning of democracy and transparency,” he said.

And Mpika North Constituency Returning Officer Donatello Singa disclosed that all poll staff in Mpika District would be deployed using road transport.

Mr Singa said arrangements for the deployment of election materials and personnel to polling stations across the district were underway.

“Residents of Mpika District should turn out in large numbers and exercise their civic right to vote on August 13,” he said.

World.title: ECZ ballot-marking contradiction sparks fresh integrity concerns
World.content:
The Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) is facing pointed questions over a contradiction in its own guidance on how voters should mark their ballots, after officials reportedly told political parties, journalists and voters that a tick is acceptable alongside the commission’s long-standing public instruction that the correct mark is an “X”. The discrepancy has emerged just a day before the country votes, against a backdrop of public allegations concerning pre-marked ballot papers.

Governance analyst Kanyanta Chanda Kapwepwe, writing in The Mast, said the commission’s current public voter education material states plainly that the correct mark is an X, and that this is the message Zambians have been officially given throughout the campaign. Yet ECZ officials are now said to be telling stakeholders that a tick, provided it remains within the box, will also be accepted.

“Yet ECZ officials are now telling political parties, journalists and voters that a tick is also acceptable provided it remains within the box. This creates an obvious and deeply troubling contradiction,” Kapwepwe wrote. The recent actions have raised further integrity concerns about the ECZ.

The concern has been sharpened by circulating public allegations that additional ballot papers were printed in Tanzania with the intention of benefiting the incumbent government, and that people hired to pre-mark those papers were allegedly given incorrect instructions on which symbol to use, resulting in ballots marked with a tick rather than an X. Tanzania’s own ballots use a tick. The allegation goes further, claiming that because it was too late to order fresh ballots once the error was discovered, the commission subsequently allowed the tick as an acceptable mark to avoid discarding the disputed papers.

Kapwepwe was careful to describe these as serious but unverified claims. “These are not trivial allegations. These are serious allegations touching the very foundation of the electoral process and bordering on electoral integrity. They demand answers from ECZ, not silence, ambiguity or contradictory instructions,” he wrote.

He argued that if no pre-marked ballots exist, the commission should have nothing to fear from issuing a clear, unequivocal clarification. If the allegations are false, he said, ECZ can and should decisively put them to rest. But if irregularities are present, he said Zambians have a right to know before entering polling stations tomorrow.

The piece calls on the commission to issue an immediate written statement matching its existing public voter-education message, warning against any scenario in which presiding officers apply inconsistent standards from one polling station to another.

“There must be no situation in which one presiding officer accepts a tick while another rejects it, or where voters in one polling station are subjected to a different standard from voters elsewhere,” Kapwepwe wrote, adding that any clarification must be published before polling begins rather than left to individual officers to interpret on the day.

This is not the only anxiety around process integrity to surface in the campaign’s closing days. Independent presidential candidate Given Katuta separately urged Zambians to guard their votes jealously, saying the electorate should not hand ballots to ECZ and walk away, arguing this creates room for what she described as underhand methods at polling stations and tallying centres.

“The electorate must not hand over ballots to the Electoral Commission of Zambia and walk away, as doing so will create room for underhand methods at polling stations and tallying centres. ECZ, in its current form, cannot conduct free and fair elections because of interference from government,” Katuta said.

Tonse-PF Pamodzi Alliance running mate Makebi Zulu made a related point, saying protecting a vote does not end with casting it, and that protection must begin at community level where people are able to vote freely without intimidation or coercion. Socialist Party national campaign manager Bob Sichinga urged all SP candidates, members and polling agents to remain vigilant throughout the process, warning that “anything is possible” once counting and transmission of results begin.

Not every party voice struck a suspicious tone. UPND media director Mark Simuuwe said his party would protect its vote in a peaceful manner consistent with what he described as the party’s hallmark approach throughout the campaign.

ECZ has not yet issued a formal public response to the marking-instruction contradiction as flagged in Kapwepwe’s analysis. With polling stations opening at 06:00 hours tomorrow and closing at 18:00 hours, the window for the commission to clarify its position before voters begin casting ballots is narrowing.
